text.p: The European Commission confirmed on Tuesday that it had cleared a joint venture between Cardo AB of Sweden and Thyssen Industrie in the field of brake systems for rail vehicles.
It said in a statement that the operation will allow the companies "to better face competition from the market leader in the sector, the German company Knorr Bremse".

Thyssen is strong in the production of discs, which is one of the components of brake systems, and has a well-established position in Germany, the Commission noted, adding that it and Cardo rather complemented each other.
The Commission also concluded that the new company and Knorr Bremse would not be able to jointly dominate the market given the existence of strong companies on the demand side.

"This market is characterised by the fact that the customers (ADtranz, Siemens, GEC Alsthom, Bombardier, Fiat ) have strong buying powers and expertise to counteract the action of the companies", the statement said.
Cardo announced on Monday in Stockholm that its joint venture with Thyssen had been cleared by the Commission. -- Brussels newsroom 322 2876841
